quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is most slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerously slick, especially right after rain begins. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush on the road to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: You can drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane if:

options.text: You are driving faster than other traffic.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
Your vehicle has more than one person in it.
You are trying to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has more than one person in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with two or more occupants. These lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement. A striped buffer zone separates them from other lanes.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let others go first, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly so other people and vehicles can move out of your way.
Must honk your horn so others know to give you space.
Must stop and go only when no people or vehicles are coming.
Can ignore people walking if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and go only when no people or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before driving onto the street from a driveway. Let any people or vehicles pass first. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: When entering a street from a private road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn cars you are entering.
Stick part of your car onto the road to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to blend with traffic smoothly.
Let pedestrians and street traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and street traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a street from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the street go first.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, drivers must account for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter noise large trucks make.
The faster speed large trucks travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not stay in a position where the truck blocks your view of traffic.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the chance of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can affect your brain and hurt your ability to drive safely. Combining alcohol with other drugs raises the risk of crashing.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other cars yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let any emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren go first.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means slow down as you approach the intersection. Let any vehicles or people in the intersection go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass, there is more risk of crashing. If you drive faster than others, you will keep having to pass. Drive with the flow of traffic, within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Hearing loss.
Air pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system moves gas out of your vehicle and keeps fumes out of the passenger area. Keep your exhaust system free of leaks to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning. Replace broken parts right away.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that cars pile up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, if you are driving so slowly that cars back up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Fog reduces how far you can see. What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive carefully and go slower.
Do not use high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, you cannot see vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals well. Drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at an intersection with multiple lanes. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Slowly move into each lane of traffic as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
The lane is shifting.
Low clearance overhead.
An extra lane is being added.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
An upcoming railroad crossing.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of a railroad crossing ahead. Drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a lane show a crosswalk. What should you know as a driver?

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must always stay out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: Your vehicle starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the other direction.
Turn your wheel toward oncoming traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both effects may become stronger.
Nothing happens.
Both effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effect becomes weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.
